page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8581C cores on the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base speed of 2.3 GHz, the processor includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The instance is equipped with 31.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores reaching top-tier classifications. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also register strong results. However, multi-core and memory subsystem performance are comparatively limited. Multi-core CPU benchmarks from stress-ng and Passmark, along with memory bandwidth tests, fall into the lower performance tiers. Database operations, such as Redis SET and Passmark database tests, also show weaker throughput.

Given the high memory density per vCPU, the c4-highmem-4 provides a specialized resource profile where memory capacity is prioritized over raw multi-threaded compute power. It is well-suited for memory-sensitive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing, such as single-threaded text processing, light caching layers, or moderate web serving. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX supports specialized vector and matrix operations, making it capable of handling light LLM prompt processing and inference tasks despite its modest core count.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is an x86_64 virtual server configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 31.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, it features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-core and text processing capabilities, alongside strong single-threaded compression speeds. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are relatively weak. This server is best suited for memory-intensive, single-threaded workloads, light web serving, and moderate database or text processing tasks where a high memory footprint is required without the need for extensive multi-core scaling.
